question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $24,$ the additive inverse of $15$ modulo $24$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $15$ modulo $24$ is the integer $0\le x<24$ such that

$$
x+15≡0\,(\text{mod}\,24).
$$

Notice that $-15+15≡0,$ so $x≡-15\,(\text{mod}\,24).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-15 & \,(\text{mod}\,24) \\  & ≡0-15 & \,(\text{mod}\,24) \\  & ≡24-15 & \,(\text{mod}\,24) \\  & ≡9 & \,(\text{mod}\,24)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $15$ modulo $24$ is $9.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
9+15≡24≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,24)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
